newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1.00 -trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1.00 -trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices were seen $0.50-$1.00 per cwt lower on Monday amid continued pressure from this week's steep skid in pork prices, livestock dealers said.
The U.S. No. 2 carcass value Thursday was quoted at $69.57 per cwt, down $3.17 from last Friday, USDA said.
Large post-holiday hog marketings and light retail demand drove pork prices lower, they said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota were seen ranging from $52.50 to $53.50 versus a top there of $54.50 quoted by USDA on Friday.
Illinois top hog prices at the plant could range from $52.00 to $52.50 and Indiana/Ohio top prices were seen at $51.00 to $52.50.

Pork price weakness was attributed to large post-holiday hog marketings and light retail demand, livestock dealers said. Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog runs Thursday totaled 114,000 head, above that day's estimate for 100,000, USDA said. Friday's estimate was 110,000 head.
Light packer demand was evident in Saturday's slaughter estimate. USDA pegged the Saturday kill at 69,000 head, well below 173,000 a week ago and 152,000 a year ago.
